title: Staging VPC Handoff Checklist (Day 1)
body:
Quick context and purpose:
- Onsite day 1 notes for staging VPC handoff to customer infra team (ACME Health).
- Goal: get baseline private control plane up, verify connectivity to customer NTP/KMS, and validate fallback behavior to Hosted API.

Site constraints / customer reminders (explicit):
- No outbound internet from control-plane VLAN (VLAN 220). All images must come from internal mirror (10.12.5.9).
- KMS: AWS CloudHSM cluster (us-east-2). Customer key alias: alias/acme-redwood. Need IAM cross-account role (role name: redwood-deploy-access).
- DNS: customer uses split-horizon. Internal hostname prefix: redwood-stg.acme.internal. Certificate chain will be provided as PEM bundle on USB.
- Firewall: only allow outbound to 10.12.5.9 (mirror), 10.12.100.1 (NTP), 10.12.200.50 (HSM proxy). All other external IPs blocked.
- MTU: network team enforces 9000 on host uplinks; confirm jumbo frames on all spine ports prior to starting.

Preflight checklist (quick run before arrival):
- [ ] Confirm internal mirror reachable: curl --head http://10.12.5.9/repo/manifest.json
- [ ] Verify KMS IAM role still present and has CA permissions
- [ ] Get cert bundle from customer, verify chain: openssl verify -CAfile chain.pem server.pem
- [ ] Bring physical media: USB with airgap image v1.4.3, USB with client certs, spare ethernet cables (blue/grey), labeled power cord (x2)
- [ ] Confirm maintenance window and contact numbers for network (NOC) and security (SecOps)

Day 1 install rough steps (order-of-ops):
1) Network & access validation (15–30m)
   - Check port mapping: ensure management NIC on mgmt VLAN (VLAN 10) has IP from dhcp range 10.10.10.128/26
   - Run: ip addr show; ping 10.12.100.1; curl http://10.12.5.9/status
2) Bring up local registry mirror if missing (use airgapped bootstrap)
   - docker run --restart unless-stopped -p 5000:5000 registry:2 + import images tarball
   - docker load < redwood-images-1.4.3.tar.gz; docker tag -> 10.12.5.9:5000/...
3) Decrypt and load certs, install to /etc/redwood/certs
   - chmod 640, chown redwood:redwood
   - update k8s secret: kubectl create secret tls redwood-tls --cert=server.pem --key=server-key.pem -n redwood-system
4) KMS/HSM tests (important)
   - Test signing: ./tools/kms-check --endpoint 10.12.200.50 --key-alias alias/acme-redwood
   - If HSM responds slowly, increase client timeout in /etc/redwood/config.yaml: hsm_timeout_ms: 12000
5) Start control plane services (systemd)
   - systemctl start redwood-controlplane.service
   - journalctl -u redwood-controlplane -f (watch for crypto init errors)
6) Health & smoke checks
   - curl -sS https://redwood-stg.acme.internal/health | jq .status (expect OK)
   - kubectl get pods -n redwood-system (all pods >= Running,READY >= 1/1)
7) Connectivity & fallback test (critical)
   - Simulate model fallback: block local model registry IP (iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.12.5.9 -j DROP) then call inference via local control plane; ensure traffic routes to Hosted API fallback (hosted-staging.redwood.com) per routing policy.
   - If fallback does not occur, check routing table: ip route show; check policy config at /etc/redwood/routing.yaml

Common blockers and quick fixes seen in previous installs:
- NTP drift causing TLS validation failures: sync with sudo chronyc -a makestep; verify chrony.conf points to 10.12.100.1
- SELinux enforced on customer hosts breaks K8s volume mounts: setenforce 0 (temporary) and log ticket for permanent policy
- Missing CA chain in cert bundle -> server cert appears fine but browsers/clients reject. Always verify fullchain.pem present and chain order correct
- HSM/proxy auth mismatch: check accepted client cert CN and ensure certificate subject matches expected principal in HSM config (case-sensitive)
- Docker registry auth failing: customer mirror requires basic auth header; get creds from SecOps vault and put in /etc/docker/daemon.json as auths

Useful commands (copy/paste):
- curl --fail --show-error -H "Host: redwood-stg.acme.internal" https://10.10.20.5/health
- journalctl -u redwood-controlplane -n 200 --no-pager | grep -i error
- sudo iptables -t nat -L -n; sudo iptables -L OUTPUT -n | grep 10.12.5.9
- kubectl -n redwood-system logs deploy/redwood-api --tail=200 | grep -E "timeout|hsm|kms|auth"

Post-handoff notes (what to hand to customer):
- Provide written list of next-steps: log retention tweak, enable metrics retention policy (14d -> 30d), set up scheduled snapshots of /var/lib/redwood (daily 02:00).
- Create follow-up ticket PD-1349 for SELinux policy work and PD-1350 for permanent mirror credentials rotation.

Contacts / who to ping during issues:
- Ben Cho (oncall infra) - Slack @bencho - pager if >30m outage
- Marcela Ruiz (security) - email marcela@acme.internal - HSM questions
- Customer NOC: +1-555-0199 (option 2), NetOps slack #acme-network

Open TODOs (for me after day 1):
- [ ] Upload final /etc/redwood/config.yaml to Confluence page and attach sanitized logs
- [ ] Push airgapped image delta to github:infra/vpc-configs PR and link to PD-1342
- [ ] Schedule follow-up remote validation in 48 hours with customer platform team

Notes to self: pack travel power-brick in top pocket, double-check hostnames match customer's ticket (they sometimes append "-dev" suffix), breathe.
